puṇḍra
(‘religious mark’)
------------------------------------------
Popular Hindu scriptures like the sectarian (minor) उपनिषद्स् and the पुराणस् ordain that every Hindu must wear a पुण्ड्र or a religious mark on the forehead as also on other parts of the body.
This पुण्ड्र may be तिर्यक्पुण्ड्र (worn crosswise) like the भस्म (or विभूति) or ऊर्ध्वपुण्ड्र like the nāma worn by the Vaiṣṇavas (followers of the विष्णु sects) or even just a tilaka (circular mark).
See TIRYAKPUṆḌRA and ŪRDHVA-PUṆḌRA for details.

puṇya
(‘that which purifies’)
------------------------------------------
The words पुण्य and पाप are commonly found in the Hindu scriptures. Even the Ṛgveda has used the words पुण्य (2.43.2) and पाप (10.164.5). So also the उपनिषद्स्.
Puṇya refers to the fruit of any good or meritorious action. Other words considered as its equivalents are: धर्म, श्रेयस्, sukṛta and vṛṣa.
Puṇya gives happiness both here and hereafter.
The most common definition of पुण्य is that which causes happiness to others, reducing their problems and difficulties.
The धर्मशास्त्रस् and the पुराणस् give detailed descriptions of पुण्य and पाप, for the guidance of people in general.

puṇyāhavācana
(‘declaring the day to be auspicious’)
------------------------------------------
Whenever an important religious rite was to be performed, it was a custom in the olden days—which prevails even today—to invite ब्राह्मणस् of erudition and pure character and take their blessings. Such an act was called ‘puṇyāhavācana’.
For instance, a person intending to perform the मर्रिअगे of his daughter, invites such ब्राह्मणस् on an auspicious day, honours them with गन्ध (sandalwood paste) and ताम्बूल (betel leaves) and declares his wish, with folded hands. The ब्राह्मणस् will respond with the words, ‘oṁ svasti,’ ‘om puṇyāham,’ and ‘om ṛddhyatām’. Each of these is to be repeated by them thrice. These phrases respectively mean: ‘May it be auspicious!’ ‘May the day be auspicious!’ ‘May the rite progress well!’
This rite seems to have been observed with regard to the performance of most of the सṁस्कारस् or sacraments.
